courts.name: Domaine des Etangs
courts.setting: A floating court on a private lake within a 13th-century château estate.
courts.blurb:
Domaine des Etangs is a 13th-century château set inside a vast private estate in the French countryside, surrounded by forests, pastures, ponds, and contemporary art. It feels less like a hotel and more like a quiet world built around nature and time.

Its tennis court is the detail that makes the place unforgettable: a floating court set on the water. Instead of a classic country-club setting, tennis here feels almost surreal — red clay, still ponds, old stone, and the silence of a château estate. A location where sport becomes part of the landscape, not separate from it.

courts.name: Monte-Carlo Country Club
courts.setting: Terraced clay courts carved into a Riviera hillside above the Mediterranean.
courts.blurb:
Monte-Carlo Country Club opened in 1928 on the edge of Monaco, though technically it sits just across the border in Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, France. That small geographical twist is part of its charm: it belongs to the Monaco myth, but its clay courts are carved into the French Riviera hillside above the Mediterranean.

The club became the permanent home of the Monte-Carlo tournament, now the Rolex Monte-Carlo Masters, one of the most elegant stops of the clay season. Its terraced courts, sea views and old Riviera atmosphere make tennis here feel less like a simple sport and more like a ritual of spring: red clay, white lines, cypress trees, and the Mediterranean just beyond the baseline.
